airport-transfer-general: Airport coaches run between Geneva airport and Val Thorens, about 3.5 hours each way. Arrival day (Sat 9 Jan) they leave Geneva at 08:30, 10:30 and 14:15, and going home (Sat 16 Jan) they leave the residences at 05:15, 07:30 and 09:30. Sign in and I'll tell you which one is yours. Times are still to be confirmed.
coach-missed: Don't panic. If you've missed your coach or your flight is delayed, message the trip WhatsApp group with your flight number and new arrival time, and a trip leader will sort out the next coach with you. Wait at arrivals if you can. (Test data.)
check-in-time: Check-in is from 17:00 on Saturday 9 January. Keys are collected from reception at your residence, and your name will be on the list. If you land early, you can drop your bags and go for lunch. (Test data.)
checkout-time: Check out by 10:00 on Saturday 16 January and hand your keys back at reception. If your coach leaves before reception opens, leave the keys in the box by the door. (Test data.)
luggage-storage: Yes, each residence has a luggage room you can use before check-in and after checkout. It's not locked, so keep valuables on you. (Test data.)
wifi: There's free wifi in all three residences. The network name and password are on the card in your room. It's good for messaging and email, but slow for streaming. (Test data.)
laundry-towels: Bed linen and towels are included in your room. Each residence has a coin-operated washing machine and dryer in the basement, so bring a few euros in coins. (Test data.)
accommodation-list: We're in three places: Résidence Village Montana (the main one, on Rue du Soleil), L'Oxalys and Le Hameau du Kashmir. Sign in and ask me where your room is and I'll tell you yours. The full details are in the Where we stay section of the guide.
cash: Card almost everywhere. Bring around €50 in cash for the odd locker, tip or taxi that isn't. There are cash machines near the Péclet shopping centre. (Test data.)
lift-pass-area: Your lift pass covers the whole Les 3 Vallées area: Val Thorens, Les Menuires, Méribel, Courchevel and more, all connected from the same lifts.
ski-lessons: Yes, lessons are available for beginners and improvers. The ski school runs group lessons each morning, and you can book them with your rentals on SkiSync. Say if you'd like to ski with other beginners from the group. (Test data.)
ski-storage: Each residence has a ski room next to the entrance where you can leave skis and boots overnight. Label them with your name, and take your boots upstairs if you want them dry. (Test data.)
piste-info: The official Val Thorens snow report and piste map show what's open and today's conditions. Both are linked in the Links section of the guide.
dress-code: No strict dress code. The themed nights ask for a costume, but it's optional and the theme is announced a day before. Warm shoes with good grip are the only must for the walk to the bars. (Test data.)
apres: The après spots on our list are in the Maps section of the guide, with a pin and a link for each. Most are right on the slopes, so you can ski straight in around 16:00.
food-grocery: There's a supermarket in the Péclet shopping centre, open every day, which is the best place for breakfast food and snacks. Prices in resort are higher than back home, so buy the basics there rather than at the shops on the slopes. (Test data.)
food-restaurants: A few good options from our list are La Chaumière, La Cabane and Chalet de la Marine. Book dinner ahead if you're a big group. The full list is under Things to do in the guide.
food-dietary: Most restaurants in resort do vegetarian dishes, and many can handle gluten-free or vegan if you ask. Tell the waiter your allergy in French or English before ordering, and message the trip WhatsApp group if you need help finding somewhere. (Test data.)
shops-gear: The ski shops around the Péclet centre and the base of the lifts sell gloves, goggles, sunscreen and the like. Expect resort prices, so pack the basics if you can. (Test data.)
activity-spa: For a spa day, try Le Spa du Val Thorens or the pools and sauna at the Le Board sports centre. Both are on the Things to do list, with links. Book ahead for a massage.
activity-rest-day: No skiing today? Plenty to do: tobogganing, snowshoeing, the spa and pools, or a long lunch on a sunny terrace. The Things to do section of the guide has them all.
activity-evening: Evenings are for dinner and après, and the week has welcome drinks, club nights and a bar crawl. The Things to do section also has night-time ideas like the pools and ice karting. Ask me what's on tonight for the plan.
phone-roaming: Most US and UK plans work in France but check your roaming charges before you fly. An eSIM for Europe is the cheapest option, and the residences have wifi. (Test data.)
power-plugs: France uses the two-round-pin European plug (type E), 230 V. US phones and laptops charge fine with a plug adapter, but check your hairdryer or other hot gear is dual-voltage. (Test data.)
